\section{Introduction}

\subsection{Two ways to be far from monotone}

A population of paired observations tells a \emph{monotone story} when higher
footprint always accompanies higher rate. On a finite index set $\iset$ with
$n = |\iset|$ and $x, y : \iset \to \R$, the pair $(i,j)$ is \emph{concordant}
when $(x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j) > 0$, \emph{discordant} when the product is
negative, and \emph{tied} when it vanishes. The population $(x,y)$ is
\emph{comonotone} when no pair is discordant:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:comono}
  (x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j) \;\ge\; 0 \qquad \text{for all } i,j \in \iset .
\end{equation}

There are two structurally distinct ways to quantify a failure of
\eqref{eq:comono}. The \emph{combinatorial} way sums the violations. Write
\[
  D(a,b) \;=\; \max\bigl(-(x_a - x_b)(y_a - y_b),\, 0\bigr) \;\ge\; 0
\]
for the \emph{discordance matrix}, which is symmetric and vanishes on the
diagonal, and set
\[
  \Delta(x,y) = \sum_{a}\sum_{b} D(a,b), \qquad
  C(x,y) = \sum_{a}\sum_{b} \max\bigl((x_a - x_b)(y_a - y_b),\, 0\bigr),
\]
the \emph{discordance mass} and the \emph{concordance mass}. Both are
nonnegative and homogeneous of degree one in $y$; and $\Delta(x,y) = 0$
characterises comonotonicity.

The \emph{geometric} way asks for the cost of a fix: perturb the rates by $d$,
pay $\|d\|_1 = \sum_i |d_i|$, and require $(x, y + d)$ to be comonotone. This is
the subject of the present paper.

\subsection{Why the comparison matters}

Given draw probabilities $p$ with $\sum_i p_i = 1$, the weighted covariance
(``the dial'')
$\wcov(p;x,y) = \sum_i p_i x_i y_i - (\sum_i p_i x_i)(\sum_j p_j y_j)$
admits the classical pair (Hoeffding) representation
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hoeffding}
  \wcov(p;x,y) \;=\; \tfrac12 \sum_i \sum_j p_i p_j (x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j).
\end{equation}
Splitting the summand into positive and negative parts yields, for
$\varepsilon \le p_i \le M$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:triage-basic}
  \tfrac12\bigl(\varepsilon^2 C(x,y) - M^2 \Delta(x,y)\bigr) \;\le\; \wcov(p;x,y),
\end{equation}
so $M^2\Delta < \varepsilon^2 C$ certifies a positive dial simultaneously for
every admissible regime: the \emph{triage rule}. Its drawback is that $\Delta$ is
a $\Theta(n^2)$-term functional of the raw pairwise table, and (Theorem
\ref{thm:notlip}) is not stable under perturbation of the rates. This paper
replaces $\Delta$ in the triage rule by a single interpretable, stable geometric
parameter, and determines exactly how much information is lost.

\section{The comonotone repair distance}

Throughout, $\iset$ is finite with $n = |\iset|$ and $x, y : \iset \to \R$.

\begin{definition}[Repair set]
The \emph{repair set} of $(x,y)$ is
\[
  \Repair(x,y) \;=\; \bigl\{ d : \iset \to \R \;\bigm|\;
    \forall i,j,\ 0 \le (x_i - x_j)\bigl((y_i + d_i) - (y_j + d_j)\bigr) \bigr\}
  \;=\; K_x - y,
\]
where $K_x = \{ z : (x,z) \text{ comonotone}\}$ is the \emph{isotonic cone} of
the preorder induced by $x$: a closed convex cone, being an intersection of
$n^2$ closed half-spaces through the origin.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonemptiness]\label{lem:nonempty}
$d = x - y \in \Repair(x,y)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
$(x_i - x_j)\bigl((y_i + x_i - y_i) - (y_j + x_j - y_j)\bigr) = (x_i - x_j)^2 \ge 0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Comonotone repair distance]
\[
  \delta(x,y) \;=\; \inf\bigl\{ \|d\|_1 : d \in \Repair(x,y) \bigr\}
  \;=\; \dist_{\ell^1}\bigl(y, K_x\bigr).
\]
\end{definition}

By Lemma \ref{lem:nonempty} the defining set is nonempty and bounded below by
$0$, so $\delta(x,y)$ is a well-defined nonnegative real.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:inf}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
  \item $\delta(x,y) \le \|d\|_1$ for every $d \in \Repair(x,y)$.
  \item If $c \le \|d\|_1$ for every $d \in \Repair(x,y)$, then $c \le \delta(x,y)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\subsection{Certificates and faithfulness}

\begin{lemma}[Pair certificate]\label{lem:cert}
If $x_i < x_j$ then $y_i - y_j \le \delta(x,y)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $d \in \Repair(x,y)$. Comonotonicity at $(i,j)$ with $x_i - x_j < 0$ forces
$(y_i + d_i) - (y_j + d_j) \le 0$, i.e.\ $y_i - y_j \le d_j - d_i$. Since $i \ne j$,
$d_j - d_i \le |d_i| + |d_j| \le \|d\|_1$. Apply Lemma \ref{lem:inf}(ii).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Faithfulness]\label{thm:faithful}
$\delta(x,y) = 0$ if and only if $(x,y)$ is comonotone.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If comonotone, $d \equiv 0$ is a repair of cost $0$. Conversely, if
$(x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j) < 0$ then $x_i \neq x_j$; assuming $x_i < x_j$ we get
$y_j < y_i$, so Lemma \ref{lem:cert} gives $0 < y_i - y_j \le \delta(x,y)$. The
case $x_j < x_i$ is symmetric.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Attainment, homogeneity, stability}

\begin{theorem}[Attainment]\label{thm:attain}
There exists $d^\star \in \Repair(x,y)$ with $\|d^\star\|_1 = \delta(x,y)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\Repair(x,y)$ is closed, being an intersection over pairs of closed sets; the
map $d \mapsto \|d\|_1$ is continuous and coercive, since $|d_i| \le \|d\|_1$.
With $B = \|x - y\|_1$, Lemma \ref{lem:nonempty} shows the infimum is unchanged
when restricted to $\Repair(x,y) \cap \{ \|d\|_\infty \le B\}$, a nonempty
compact set, on which a continuous function attains its minimum.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Positive homogeneity]\label{thm:homog}
For $c \ge 0$, $\delta(x, c\,y) = c\,\delta(x,y)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $c > 0$, $d \mapsto c\,d$ is a bijection $\Repair(x,y) \to \Repair(x, cy)$
(the constraints are positively homogeneous) scaling the cost by $c$. For $c=0$
the rates are constant, hence comonotone, and both sides vanish by Theorem
\ref{thm:faithful}.
\end{proof}

Since $\Delta(x, c y) = c\,\Delta(x,y)$ as well, \emph{both defect functionals are
homogeneous of degree one in the rates}; this kills the conjecture
$\delta^2 \le \Delta$ in Section \ref{sec:refute}.

\begin{theorem}[One-sided stability]\label{thm:onesided}
$\delta(x,y) \le \delta(x,y') + \|y - y'\|_1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If $d \in \Repair(x,y')$ then $d + (y' - y) \in \Repair(x,y)$, since
$y + (d + y' - y) = y' + d$ is comonotone with $x$. The triangle inequality gives
$\|d + (y' - y)\|_1 \le \|d\|_1 + \|y - y'\|_1$, so
$\delta(x,y) - \|y - y'\|_1 \le \|d\|_1$ for all $d \in \Repair(x,y')$; conclude
by Lemma \ref{lem:inf}(ii).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[$1$-Lipschitz]\label{cor:lip}
$\bigl|\delta(x,y) - \delta(x,y')\bigr| \le \|y - y'\|_1$.
\end{corollary}

\section{The upper bound}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound]\label{thm:upper}
If $|x_i - x_j| \le R$ for all $i,j$, then
$\Delta(x,y) \le 2\,n\,R\,\delta(x,y)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Fix $d \in \Repair(x,y)$ and a pair $(i,j)$. Comonotonicity of $(x, y+d)$ gives
$0 \le (x_i - x_j)\bigl((y_i - y_j) + (d_i - d_j)\bigr)$, hence
\[
  -(x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j) \;\le\; (x_i - x_j)(d_i - d_j)
  \;\le\; |x_i - x_j|\,|d_i - d_j| \;\le\; R\bigl(|d_i| + |d_j|\bigr).
\]
The right side is nonnegative, so it also dominates $0$; therefore
$D(i,j) \le R(|d_i| + |d_j|)$. Summing over all ordered pairs and using
$\sum_i \sum_j (|d_i| + |d_j|) = 2 n \|d\|_1$ gives
$\Delta(x,y) \le 2 n R \|d\|_1$. Taking the infimum over $d$ (the cases $n = 0$
and $R = 0$ being trivial) completes the proof.
\end{proof}

Every coordinate $|d_k|$ is charged $2n$ times, once for each pair in which it
appears; this double counting is the source of the factor $n$, which Theorem
\ref{thm:nsharp} shows is necessary.

\section{The sharp lower bound via the isotonic upper envelope}

\begin{definition}[$g$-separation]
The footprint $x$ is \emph{$g$-separated} ($g>0$) if $x_i < x_j$ implies
$x_j - x_i \ge g$.
\end{definition}

Dose levels, grade bands, integer counts, and any footprint valued in a fixed
finite grid are $g$-separated.

\begin{definition}[Predecessor set and isotonic upper envelope]
For $i \in \iset$ set
$P(i) = \{i\} \cup \{ j : x_j < x_i \}$ and
$\hat y_i = \max_{j \in P(i)} y_j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:env}
$y_i \le \hat y_i$ for all $i$; $x_i < x_k$ implies $\hat y_i \le \hat y_k$; and
$(x, \hat y)$ is comonotone.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The first claim holds since $i \in P(i)$. For the second, $x_i < x_k$ gives
$P(i) \subseteq P(k)$ (indeed $i \in P(k)$, and $x_j < x_i < x_k$ gives
$j \in P(k)$), and a maximum over a larger set is larger. For the third: if
$x_i < x_j$ then both factors of $(x_i - x_j)(\hat y_i - \hat y_j)$ are
nonpositive; the case $x_j < x_i$ is symmetric; and if $x_i = x_j$ the product
vanishes.
\end{proof}

Hence $d^{\mathrm{env}} = \hat y - y \ge 0$ is an admissible repair, and with
$\cost(b) = \hat y_b - y_b \ge 0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:envbound}
  \delta(x,y) \;\le\; \sum_b \cost(b).
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Witness]\label{lem:witness}
For each $b$ choose $w(b) \in P(b)$ with $\hat y_b = y_{w(b)}$. If
$\cost(b) > 0$ then $x_{w(b)} < x_b$ and $y_b < y_{w(b)}$, so the ordered pair
$(w(b), b)$ is discordant.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
$\cost(b) > 0$ gives $y_b < y_{w(b)}$, hence $w(b) \ne b$, hence
$w(b) \in P(b) \setminus\{b\}$, i.e.\ $x_{w(b)} < x_b$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Charge]\label{lem:charge}
If $x$ is $g$-separated and $\cost(b) > 0$, then
$g \cdot \cost(b) \le D(w(b), b)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By Lemma \ref{lem:witness} and $g$-separation, $x_b - x_{w(b)} \ge g$ and
$y_{w(b)} - y_b = \cost(b) > 0$, so
$D(w(b),b) = (x_b - x_{w(b)})(y_{w(b)} - y_b) \ge g\,\cost(b)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension-free lower bound]\label{thm:lower}
If $x$ is $g$-separated, then $g\,\delta(x,y) \le \Delta(x,y)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The inequality $g\,\cost(b) \le \sum_a D(a,b)$ holds by Lemma \ref{lem:charge}
when $\cost(b) > 0$ and trivially otherwise. Summing over $b$ and using
\eqref{eq:envbound},
$g\,\delta(x,y) \le \sum_b \sum_a D(a,b) = \Delta(x,y)$.
\end{proof}

The charge for key $b$ lands in \emph{column} $b$ of the discordance matrix;
distinct keys therefore consume disjoint columns, and the charges sum without
loss. This is what makes the bound dimension free.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp lower bound]\label{thm:sharplower}
If $x$ is $g$-separated, then $2\,g\,\delta(x,y) \le \Delta(x,y)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Write $\Delta(x,y) = \sum_{(a,b)} D(a,b)$ as a sum over ordered pairs, and
consider the families
$\mathcal{F} = \{(w(b), b)\}$ and $\mathcal{F}^\top = \{(b, w(b))\}$, indexed by
the keys $b$ with $\cost(b) > 0$. Each family is injectively indexed by $b$ (the
second, resp.\ first, coordinate is $b$). The families are disjoint: an overlap
$(w(b), b) = (b', w(b'))$ would give $x_{b'} = x_{w(b)} < x_b$ and
$x_b = x_{w(b')} < x_{b'}$, a contradiction. Since $D$ is symmetric,
$D(b, w(b)) = D(w(b), b) \ge g\,\cost(b)$ by Lemma \ref{lem:charge}. Summing over
$\mathcal{F} \sqcup \mathcal{F}^\top$, whose index pairs are pairwise distinct and
all remaining entries of $D$ nonnegative, gives
$2 g \sum_b \cost(b) \le \Delta(x,y)$; conclude by \eqref{eq:envbound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Optimality of the constant $2$]\label{thm:optconst}
The constant $2$ in Theorem \ref{thm:sharplower} cannot be increased. For the
$1$-separated two-key population $x = (0,1)$, $y = (3,0)$ one has $g = 1$,
$\delta = 3$ and $\Delta = 6$, so $2 g \delta = \Delta$; hence for every $C > 2$
the inequality $C g \delta \le \Delta$ fails.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The only discordant unordered pair is $\{0,1\}$, with violation
$-(0-1)(3-0) = 3$, counted twice among ordered pairs, so $\Delta = 6$. The
perturbation $d = (-3,0)$ flattens the rates, so $\delta \le 3$; and Lemma
\ref{lem:cert} on $(0,1)$ gives $3 \le \delta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp two-sided comparison]\label{thm:twosided}
Let $x$ be $g$-separated with $|x_i - x_j| \le R$ for all $i,j$, on $n$ keys.
Then
\[
  2\,g\,\delta(x,y) \;\le\; \Delta(x,y) \;\le\; 2\,n\,R\,\delta(x,y).
\]
The left constant is attained; the right bound is attained up to a factor of two
and its factor $n$ cannot be removed.
\end{theorem}

\section{Refutations and sharpness}\label{sec:refute}

The literal dimension-free conjecture
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj}
  \delta^2 \;\le\; \Delta \;\le\; 2\,\delta\,R
\end{equation}
is false on both sides.

\begin{theorem}[No quadratic lower bound]\label{thm:noquad}
The inequality $\delta(x,y)^2 \le \Delta(x,y)$ fails in general: for $x = (0,1)$,
$y = (3,0)$ one has $\delta^2 = 9 > 6 = \Delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No superlinear comparison]\label{thm:nosuper}
For every constant $C$ there is a population with
$C \cdot \Delta(x,y) < \delta(x,y)^2$. Take $x = (0,1)$ and $y_t = (3t, 0)$ for
$t > 0$: then $\delta = 3t$, $\Delta = 6t$, and
$\delta^2/\Delta = 3t/2 \to \infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
The failure is structural. Both $\Delta$ and $\delta$ are positively homogeneous
of degree one in the rates, while $\delta^2$ is homogeneous of degree two. No
inequality between a degree-two and a degree-one positive functional can hold on
a scaling-closed family unless the degree-two side vanishes identically. Any
correct comparison must be degree matched, which is exactly what Theorem
\ref{thm:twosided} delivers.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[No dimension-free upper bound]\label{thm:nodimfree}
The inequality $\Delta \le 2\,\delta\,R$ fails in general: for $x = (0,1,2)$,
$y = (1,0,0)$ one has $R = 2$, $\delta = 1$ and $\Delta = 6 > 4$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The discordant unordered pairs are $\{0,1\}$ with violation $-(0-1)(1-0) = 1$ and
$\{0,2\}$ with violation $-(0-2)(1-0) = 2$; the pair $\{1,2\}$ is tied. Doubling
for ordered pairs, $\Delta = 6$. The perturbation $d = (-1,0,0)$ flattens the
rates, so $\delta \le 1$, and Lemma \ref{lem:cert} on $(0,1)$ gives $1 \le \delta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Outlier family]
For $m \ge 0$ and $n = m+2$ keys indexed $0, \dots, n-1$, set
$x^{(m)}_i = i$ and $y^{(m)}_i = 1$ if $i = 0$, else $0$. The footprint is
$1$-separated with range $R = n - 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact values on the outlier family]\label{thm:family}
$\Delta(x^{(m)}, y^{(m)}) = n(n-1)$ and $\delta(x^{(m)}, y^{(m)}) = 1$; hence
$\Delta = \tfrac12 \bigl(2 n R \delta\bigr)$, so the bound of Theorem
\ref{thm:upper} overshoots by exactly a factor of two on this family.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The discordant unordered pairs are exactly $\{0,j\}$, $j \ge 1$, with violation
$-(0-j)(1-0) = j$; hence $\Delta = 2\sum_{j=1}^{n-1} j = n(n-1)$. Lowering the
outlier, $d = (-1,0,\dots,0)$, flattens the rates, so $\delta \le 1$; Lemma
\ref{lem:cert} on $(0,1)$ gives $1 \le \delta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The population-size factor is necessary]\label{thm:nsharp}
For every constant $C$ there is a member of the outlier family with
$C \cdot R\,\delta < \Delta$: indeed $\Delta/(R\delta) = n$, which is unbounded.
Hence no inequality of the form $\Delta \le C R \delta$ holds, and the factor $n$
in Theorem \ref{thm:upper} is unavoidable.
\end{theorem}

\section{Applications: triage, robustness, and the dial}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform pair identity]\label{thm:pairid}
For $n \ge 1$ and uniform weights $p_i \equiv 1/n$,
\[
  2\,n^2 \cdot \wcov(p; x, y) \;=\; C(x,y) - \Delta(x,y).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By \eqref{eq:hoeffding} with $p_i = 1/n$,
$\wcov = \tfrac{1}{2n^2}\sum_i\sum_j (x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j)$, and splitting each
summand into positive and negative parts gives
$\sum_i\sum_j (x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j) = C(x,y) - \Delta(x,y)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Regime-uniform positivity]\label{thm:triagebasic}
Suppose $\sum_i p_i = 1$ and $\varepsilon \le p_i \le M$ with $\varepsilon > 0$.
If $M^2 \Delta(x,y) < \varepsilon^2 C(x,y)$ then $\wcov(p;x,y) > 0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Split \eqref{eq:hoeffding} into concordant and discordant contributions: each
concordant term is at least $\varepsilon^2$ times the corresponding concordance
entry, each discordant term at least $-M^2$ times the corresponding entry of $D$.
This gives \eqref{eq:triage-basic}, whose right side is positive by hypothesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Triage from the repair distance]\label{thm:triagerepair}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:triagebasic}, with $|x_i - x_j| \le R$,
the conclusion $\wcov(p;x,y) > 0$ holds as soon as
\[
  M^2 \cdot \bigl(2 n R\,\delta(x,y)\bigr) \;<\; \varepsilon^2 C(x,y),
  \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
  \kappa^2 \cdot 2 n R\,\delta(x,y) \;<\; C(x,y),
\]
where $\kappa = M/\varepsilon$ is the conditioning number of the regime.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem \ref{thm:upper} gives $\Delta \le 2 n R \delta$; multiply by $M^2 \ge 0$
and apply Theorem \ref{thm:triagebasic}.
\end{proof}

A population that is cheap to repair cannot be triaged away by any conditioning
number: for fixed $C > 0$ the rule fires for all regimes as soon as
$\delta < C/(2\kappa^2 n R)$.

\begin{theorem}[The discordance mass is not Lipschitz]\label{thm:notlip}
The estimate $|\Delta(x,y) - \Delta(x,y')| \le \|y - y'\|_1$ fails: for
$x = (0,1)$, comparing $y = (3,0)$ with the flat vector $y' = (0,0)$ gives
$\|y-y'\|_1 = 3$ while $|\Delta(x,y) - \Delta(x,y')| = 6$. Moreover no universal
Lipschitz constant exists: with $x^{(\lambda)} = (0,\lambda)$ and the fixed
displacement $y = (3,0)$, $y' = (2,0)$ of size $1$, one has
$|\Delta(x^{(\lambda)},y) - \Delta(x^{(\lambda)},y')| = 2\lambda \to \infty$.
\end{theorem}

By contrast $\delta$ is $1$-Lipschitz (Corollary \ref{cor:lip}). Since rate
vectors are measured rather than given, a statistic whose sensitivity grows with
the magnitude of the data cannot support a certificate; the repair distance can.

\begin{theorem}[Robust triage]\label{thm:robust}
Suppose the true rate vector is $y$, the measured one is $y'$, and
$\|y - y'\|_1 \le \eta$. Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:triagerepair},
if
$M^2 \bigl(2 n R (\delta(x,y') + \eta)\bigr) < \varepsilon^2 C(x,y)$
then $\wcov(p;x,y) > 0$ for every admissible regime.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Corollary \ref{cor:lip} gives $\delta(x,y) \le \delta(x,y') + \eta$; substitute
into Theorem \ref{thm:triagerepair}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The repair distance caps the dial]\label{thm:cap}
Let $x$ be $g$-separated and $p$ uniform on $n \ge 1$ keys. Then
\[
  2 n^2 \wcov(p;x,y) \;\le\; C(x,y) - g\,\delta(x,y),
  \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
  g\,\delta(x,y) \;\le\; C(x,y) - 2 n^2 \wcov(p;x,y).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem \ref{thm:pairid} gives $2n^2 \wcov = C - \Delta$ and Theorem
\ref{thm:lower} gives $g\delta \le \Delta$.
\end{proof}

Operationally, the amount of $\ell^1$ repair a population needs is subtracted,
one for one up to the separation constant, from the largest dial reading it can
possibly produce; conversely a strong observed association certifies that the
underlying data is cheap to make monotone. Using Theorem \ref{thm:sharplower} in
place of Theorem \ref{thm:lower} doubles the budget term.

\section{Irreducibility}

\begin{theorem}[Irreducibility]\label{thm:irred}
There exist two populations with the same footprint and the same repair distance
but different discordance masses. With $x = (0,1,2)$,
\[
  y = (1,0,0): \ \delta = 1,\ \Delta = 6; \qquad
  y' = (0,1,0): \ \delta = 1,\ \Delta = 2 .
\]
Hence $\Delta$ is not a function of $\delta$, even after fixing $x$, $n$, $g$ and
$R$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The values for $y$ are Theorem \ref{thm:nodimfree}. For $y'$, the only discordant
unordered pair is $\{1,2\}$, with violation $-(1-2)(1-0) = 1$, so $\Delta = 2$;
the pair $\{0,1\}$ is concordant and $\{0,2\}$ tied. The perturbation
$d = (0,-1,0)$ flattens the rates, so $\delta \le 1$, and Lemma \ref{lem:cert} on
$(1,2)$ gives $1 \le \delta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
An $\ell^1$ repair records only \emph{how far} rates must move; the discordance
mass additionally records \emph{how many pairs} each misplaced rate offends, a
count depending on the offending key's position in the footprint order. An
outlier at the extreme of the order is discordant with $\Theta(n)$ pairs; an
inversion between order-neighbours with one. Both cost one unit of $\ell^1$
repair. Consequently: the two-sided comparison cannot be sharpened to an
identity; the triage rule of Theorem \ref{thm:triagerepair} is strictly weaker
than the exact criterion of Theorem \ref{thm:triagebasic}; and the pairwise data
is irreducible in the precise sense that it carries information invisible to any
$\ell^1$ repair statistic.
\end{remark}

\section{Algorithms and computation}

Both masses are direct $O(n^2)$ computations over ordered pairs. For the repair
distance, the envelope of Lemma \ref{lem:env} gives an $O(n^2)$ (indeed
sorting-based, $O(n \log n)$) upper bound with a constructive certificate, and
the pair certificates of Lemma \ref{lem:cert} give the $O(n^2)$ lower bound
$\max\{ y_i - y_j : x_i < x_j\}$; on the two-key witness and on the outlier
family these coincide, which is how the exact values above were obtained.

In general $\delta(x,y) = \min_{z \in K_x}\|y - z\|_1$ is an $\ell^1$ isotonic
regression, a linear program in $n$ variables. Since the objective is piecewise
linear on the polyhedral cone $K_x$, the minimum is attained at a vertex of the
feasible region translated by $y$, and every such vertex has coordinates drawn
from the multiset of observed rates. This yields a finite search --- the
\emph{$\ell^1$ isotonic normal form} --- and, in the totally ordered case, a
dynamic program over levels $\ell$ and candidate values $v$ from the sorted rate
multiset:
\[
  F(\ell, v) \;=\; \min_{v' \le v} F(\ell - 1, v') \;+\; \sum_{i \text{ at level } \ell} |y_i - v|,
  \qquad F(0,\cdot) \equiv 0 .
\]

The triage certificate is then decided by computing $R$, the separation $g$, the
concordance mass $C$, and any upper bound on $\delta$, and reporting
\emph{certified} when $(M/\varepsilon)^2 \cdot 2 n R (\delta + \eta) < C$. An
upper bound suffices, which is what makes the envelope operationally useful.

\section{Future directions}

\paragraph{Exact $\ell^1$ isotonic normal form.}
The vertex characterisation above is folklore for $\ell^1$ isotonic regression
but is not established here. Attainment (Theorem \ref{thm:attain}) gives
\emph{some} minimiser; the remaining step is a purely combinatorial vertex
argument showing that some minimiser has all coordinates drawn from the multiset
of observed rates. This would make $\delta$ a computable statistic in the strict
sense and enable decision-procedure-level certification of triage rules on
concrete populations.

\paragraph{Weighted repair distance and regime-dependent triage.}
The triage rule of Theorem \ref{thm:triagerepair} is regime uniform and the
conditioning number enters as $\kappa^2$. Replacing the $\ell^1$ cost by the
regime-weighted cost $\sum_i p_i |d_i|$ should reduce this to $\kappa$: both the
discordance mass and the repair cost are charged pair by pair, so charging each
key by its own draw mass keeps the disjoint double-charging argument of Theorem
\ref{thm:sharplower} intact while replacing one factor of $\kappa$ by an exact
weight.

\paragraph{Which repair costs recover the pairwise data?}
Theorem \ref{thm:irred} shows the unweighted $\ell^1$ cost loses the count of
offended pairs. One would like the exact class of costs $\sum_i c_i |d_i|$, with
$c_i$ depending on the rank of $i$ in the footprint order, for which the
comparison becomes an identity or the triage rule becomes necessary as well as
sufficient. A negative answer would be an even stronger irreducibility theorem.

\paragraph{Further questions.}
A matching lower bound for footprints that are not $g$-separated, using a modulus
of separation; continuous-population analogues where the envelope becomes a
running supremum; and an $\ell^2$ analogue where the envelope is replaced by the
pool-adjacent-violators projection and the charging argument must account for
averaging rather than maximisation.

\section{Conclusion}

The comonotone repair distance --- the least $\ell^1$ perturbation of the rates
removing every discordant pair --- stands in sharp two-sided relation with the
discordance mass, $2 g \delta \le \Delta \le 2 n R \delta$, with the left constant
exactly optimal, the right sharp up to a factor of two, and the population-size
factor provably necessary. The natural dimension-free conjecture
$\delta^2 \le \Delta \le 2\delta R$ is false in both directions, for a degree
reason and a dimension reason respectively. The comparison converts the
regime-uniform triage criterion for a positive weighted covariance into a
criterion in a single interpretable, measurement-robust parameter, and exhibits
that parameter as a budget line inside the covariance itself. Its limit is
equally precise: two populations with the same footprint and the same repair
distance can have discordance masses differing by a factor of three, so the
pairwise table is not compressible into any $\ell^1$ repair statistic.

Comonotone Repair Distance vs. Discordance Mass
===============================================

Numerical companion to "The Comonotone Repair Distance and the Discordance Mass".

Everything here is self-contained: no third-party dependencies, only the standard
library.  We compute, for finite populations (x, y) of paired observations,

    *  the discordance mass      Delta(x, y) = sum_{i,j} max(-(x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j), 0)
    *  the concordance mass      C(x, y)     = sum_{i,j} max( (x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j), 0)
    *  the weighted covariance   wcov(p;x,y) = (1/2) sum_{i,j} p_i p_j (x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j)
    *  the repair distance       delta(x, y) = min { ||d||_1 : (x, y+d) comonotone }

and we verify numerically:

    1.  the uniform pair identity        2 n^2 wcov = C - Delta
    2.  the sharp two-sided comparison   2 g delta <= Delta <= 2 n R delta
    3.  attainment of the constant 2     (x = (0,1), y = (3,0))
    4.  failure of  delta^2 <= Delta     (a degree obstruction)
    5.  failure of  Delta <= 2 delta R   (a dimension obstruction)
    6.  irreducibility: Delta is not a function of delta
    7.  the regime-uniform triage rule and its measurement-robust version
    8.  the dial cap  2 n^2 wcov <= C - g delta

Run with:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Vector = Sequence[float]

TOL: float = 1e-9


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pairwise functionals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def discordance_mass(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Sum over ORDERED pairs of the size of each violation of comonotonicity."""
    return sum(
        max(-(x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j]), 0.0)
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def concordance_mass(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Sum over ORDERED pairs of the size of each agreement."""
    return sum(
        max((x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j]), 0.0)
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def wcov(p: Vector, x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Weighted covariance in its pair (Hoeffding) form."""
    return 0.5 * sum(
        p[i] * p[j] * (x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j])
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def is_comonotone(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> bool:
    """True when no ordered pair is discordant."""
    return all(
        (x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j]) >= -TOL
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def footprint_range(x: Vector) -> float:
    """R = max_{i,j} |x_i - x_j|."""
    return max(x) - min(x) if x else 0.0


def footprint_separation(x: Vector) -> float:
    """g = min { x_j - x_i : x_i < x_j }, or +inf when x is constant."""
    values = sorted(set(x))
    if len(values) < 2:
        return float("inf")
    return min(b - a for a, b in zip(values, values[1:]))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The repair distance: bounds and exact value
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def isotonic_upper_envelope(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> List[float]:
    """Largest rate observed at or strictly below each key's footprint.

    This is the canonical isotonic majorant of y along x; it is comonotone with
    x, so the nonnegative nudge (envelope - y) is always an admissible repair.
    """
    n = len(x)
    return [
        max(y[j] for j in range(n) if j == i or x[j] < x[i])
        for i in range(n)
    ]


def envelope_repair_cost(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Constructive UPPER bound on delta given by the isotonic upper envelope."""
    env = isotonic_upper_envelope(x, y)
    return sum(e - v for e, v in zip(env, y))


def pair_certificate_bound(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """LOWER bound on delta: the largest single inversion of the rates.

    If x_i < x_j then any repair must close the gap y_i - y_j, so this maximum
    is a valid lower bound for the repair distance.
    """
    n = len(x)
    best = 0.0
    for i, j in product(range(n), repeat=2):
        if x[i] < x[j]:
            best = max(best, y[i] - y[j])
    return best


def repair_distance(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Exact comonotone repair distance delta(x, y).

    delta(x, y) = min { ||y - z||_1 : (x, z) comonotone }.  Keys sharing a
    footprint value impose no constraint on each other, so the feasible z are
    exactly those admitting cuts t_0 <= t_1 <= ... with every rate at level l
    lying in [t_{l-1}, t_l].  The objective is piecewise linear, so an optimal
    set of cuts may be taken from the multiset of observed rates; a dynamic
    program over (level, cut) then gives the exact optimum.
    """
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0

    levels: Dict[float, List[float]] = {}
    for xi, yi in zip(x, y):
        levels.setdefault(xi, []).append(yi)
    blocks: List[List[float]] = [levels[v] for v in sorted(levels)]

    cuts: List[float] = sorted(set(y))
    k = len(cuts)

    def block_cost(block: Sequence[float], low: float, high: float) -> float:
        """Cost of clamping every rate of a level into the interval [low, high]."""
        return sum(max(low - v, 0.0) + max(v - high, 0.0) for v in block)

    low0 = cuts[0]  # optimal rates never leave [min y, max y]
    table: List[float] = [block_cost(blocks[0], low0, cuts[c]) for c in range(k)]

    for block in blocks[1:]:
        new_table = [float("inf")] * k
        for c in range(k):                      # ceiling of this level
            best = float("inf")
            for c_prev in range(c + 1):         # floor inherited from below
                candidate = table[c_prev] + block_cost(block, cuts[c_prev], cuts[c])
                best = min(best, candidate)
            new_table[c] = best
        table = new_table

    return min(table)


def optimal_repair(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> List[float]:
    """An optimal perturbation d with ||d||_1 = delta(x, y), found by search
    over cut vectors drawn from the observed rates (attainment made explicit)."""
    n = len(x)
    levels: Dict[float, List[int]] = {}
    for i, xi in enumerate(x):
        levels.setdefault(xi, []).append(i)
    blocks: List[List[int]] = [levels[v] for v in sorted(levels)]
    cuts: List[float] = sorted(set(y))

    best_cost = float("inf")
    best_z: List[float] = list(y)
    for choice in product(range(len(cuts)), repeat=len(blocks)):
        if any(a > b for a, b in zip(choice, choice[1:])):
            continue
        z = list(y)
        low = cuts[0]
        cost = 0.0
        for block, c in zip(blocks, choice):
            high = cuts[c]
            for i in block:
                zi = min(max(y[i], low), high)
                z[i] = zi
                cost += abs(zi - y[i])
            low = high
        if cost < best_cost - TOL:
            best_cost, best_z = cost, z
    return [zi - yi for zi, yi in zip(best_z, y)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Triage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def triage_certified(
    x: Vector, y: Vector, eps: float, big_m: float, eta: float = 0.0
) -> bool:
    """Regime-uniform triage from the single population parameter delta.

    Returns True when  (M/eps)^2 * 2 n R (delta + eta) < C(x, y), which
    certifies wcov(p; x, y) > 0 for EVERY draw regime with eps <= p_i <= M,
    tolerating total measurement error eta in the rates.
    """
    n = len(x)
    kappa = big_m / eps
    budget = kappa ** 2 * 2 * n * footprint_range(x) * (repair_distance(x, y) + eta)
    return budget < concordance_mass(x, y)


def worst_case_wcov(x: Vector, y: Vector, eps: float, big_m: float,
                    trials: int = 20000, seed: int = 0) -> float:
    """Smallest weighted covariance found by random search over admissible
    regimes eps <= p_i <= M, sum p_i = 1.  Used to sanity-check triage."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = len(x)
    worst = float("inf")
    for _ in range(trials):
        raw = [rng.random() for _ in range(n)]
        total = sum(raw)
        p = [r / total for r in raw]
        if all(eps - TOL <= pi <= big_m + TOL for pi in p):
            worst = min(worst, wcov(p, x, y))
    return worst


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 74)


def report_population(name: str, x: Vector, y: Vector) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    delta = repair_distance(x, y)
    delta_mass = discordance_mass(x, y)
    conc = concordance_mass(x, y)
    n = len(x)
    R = footprint_range(x)
    g = footprint_separation(x)
    env = envelope_repair_cost(x, y)
    cert = pair_certificate_bound(x, y)
    print(f"\n{name}")
    print(f"  x = {list(x)}")
    print(f"  y = {list(y)}")
    print(f"  n = {n}   range R = {R:g}   separation g = {g:g}")
    print(f"  discordance mass  Delta = {delta_mass:g}")
    print(f"  concordance mass  C     = {conc:g}")
    print(f"  repair distance   delta = {delta:g}"
          f"   (certificate {cert:g} <= delta <= envelope {env:g})")
    if g < float("inf"):
        lhs, rhs = 2 * g * delta, 2 * n * R * delta
        ok = lhs <= delta_mass + TOL <= rhs + TOL
        print(f"  two-sided:  2g*delta = {lhs:g}  <=  Delta = {delta_mass:g}"
              f"  <=  2nR*delta = {rhs:g}   [{'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}]")
    return delta, delta_mass

    banner("2.  The constant 2 in  2 g delta <= Delta  is exactly attained")
    x, y = [0.0, 1.0], [3.0, 0.0]

    delta = repair_distance(x, y)
    mass = discordance_mass(x, y)
    print(f"\n  x = {x},  y = {y}")
    print(f"  g = {g:g},  delta = {delta:g},  Delta = {mass:g}")

        print(f"  {t:>8g} {d:>10g} {m:>10g} {d * d / m:>16g}")
    print("\n  The ratio grows linearly in t, so no constant C satisfies")

def demo_dimension_obstruction() -> None:
    banner("4.  Delta <= 2 delta R is false: the population-size factor is needed")
    print("\n  Outlier family: x = (0,1,...,n-1), y = (1,0,...,0).")
    print(f"\n  {'n':>4} {'delta':>8} {'R':>6} {'Delta':>10} "
          f"{'2 delta R':>12} {'Delta/(R delta)':>17} {'2 n R delta':>13}")
    for n in range(2, 10):
        x = [float(i) for i in range(n)]
        y = [1.0] + [0.0] * (n - 1)
        d = repair_distance(x, y)
        m = discordance_mass(x, y)
        R = footprint_range(x)
        print(f"  {n:>4} {d:>8g} {R:>6g} {m:>10g} {2 * d * R:>12g} "

    print("\n  Delta = n(n-1) exactly, so Delta/(R delta) = n is unbounded:")

    x = [0.0, 1.0, 2.0]

        print(f"\n  y = {y}  ({label})")
        print(f"    delta = {repair_distance(x, y):g}")
        print(f"    Delta = {discordance_mass(x, y):g}")
    print("\n  Same footprint, same repair distance, discordance masses 6 and 2.")
    print("  An l^1 repair sees how far rates must move, not how many pairs each")

def demo_pair_identity_and_cap() -> None:
    banner("6.  The uniform pair identity and the dial cap")
    populations = [
        ([0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0], [0.0, 2.0, 1.0, 4.0]),
        ([0.0, 1.0, 2.0], [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
        ([0.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0], [1.0, 3.0, 2.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
    ]
    for x, y in populations:
        n = len(x)
        p = [1.0 / n] * n
        lhs = 2 * n ** 2 * wcov(p, x, y)
        rhs = concordance_mass(x, y) - discordance_mass(x, y)
        g = footprint_separation(x)
        delta = repair_distance(x, y)
        cap = concordance_mass(x, y) - g * delta

    for _ in range(4000):
        n = rng.randint(2, 7)
        x = [float(rng.randint(0, 5)) for _ in range(n)]
        y = [float(rng.randint(-4, 4)) for _ in range(n)]
        g = footprint_separation(x)
        if g == float("inf"):
            continue
        R = footprint_range(x)
        delta = repair_distance(x, y)
        mass = discordance_mass(x, y)
        assert 2 * g * delta <= mass + 1e-7, (x, y)
        assert mass <= 2 * n * R * delta + 1e-7, (x, y)
        # also check the envelope / certificate sandwich and Lipschitz stability
        assert pair_certificate_bound(x, y) <= delta + 1e-9

    print("    2 g delta <= Delta <= 2 n R delta,")
    print("    max single inversion <= delta <= envelope cost,")

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Vector = Sequence[float]

TOL: float = 1e-9


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pairwise functionals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def discordance_mass(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Sum over ORDERED pairs of the size of each violation of comonotonicity."""
    return sum(
        max(-(x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j]), 0.0)
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def concordance_mass(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Sum over ORDERED pairs of the size of each agreement."""
    return sum(
        max((x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j]), 0.0)
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def wcov(p: Vector, x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Weighted covariance in its pair (Hoeffding) form."""
    return 0.5 * sum(
        p[i] * p[j] * (x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j])
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def is_comonotone(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> bool:
    """True when no ordered pair is discordant."""
    return all(
        (x[i] - x[j]) * (y[i] - y[j]) >= -TOL
        for i, j in product(range(len(x)), repeat=2)
    )


def footprint_range(x: Vector) -> float:
    """R = max_{i,j} |x_i - x_j|."""
    return max(x) - min(x) if x else 0.0


def footprint_separation(x: Vector) -> float:
    """g = min { x_j - x_i : x_i < x_j }, or +inf when x is constant."""
    values = sorted(set(x))
    if len(values) < 2:
        return float("inf")
    return min(b - a for a, b in zip(values, values[1:]))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The repair distance: bounds and exact value
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def isotonic_upper_envelope(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> List[float]:
    """Largest rate observed at or strictly below each key's footprint.

    This is the canonical isotonic majorant of y along x; it is comonotone with
    x, so the nonnegative nudge (envelope - y) is always an admissible repair.
    """
    n = len(x)
    return [
        max(y[j] for j in range(n) if j == i or x[j] < x[i])
        for i in range(n)
    ]


def envelope_repair_cost(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Constructive UPPER bound on delta given by the isotonic upper envelope."""
    env = isotonic_upper_envelope(x, y)
    return sum(e - v for e, v in zip(env, y))


def pair_certificate_bound(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """LOWER bound on delta: the largest single inversion of the rates.

    If x_i < x_j then any repair must close the gap y_i - y_j, so this maximum
    is a valid lower bound for the repair distance.
    """
    n = len(x)
    best = 0.0
    for i, j in product(range(n), repeat=2):
        if x[i] < x[j]:
            best = max(best, y[i] - y[j])
    return best


def repair_distance(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Exact comonotone repair distance delta(x, y).

    delta(x, y) = min { ||y - z||_1 : (x, z) comonotone }.  Keys sharing a
    footprint value impose no constraint on each other, so the feasible z are
    exactly those admitting cuts t_0 <= t_1 <= ... with every rate at level l
    lying in [t_{l-1}, t_l].  The objective is piecewise linear, so an optimal
    set of cuts may be taken from the multiset of observed rates; a dynamic
    program over (level, cut) then gives the exact optimum.
    """
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0

    levels: Dict[float, List[float]] = {}
    for xi, yi in zip(x, y):
        levels.setdefault(xi, []).append(yi)
    blocks: List[List[float]] = [levels[v] for v in sorted(levels)]

    cuts: List[float] = sorted(set(y))
    k = len(cuts)

    def block_cost(block: Sequence[float], low: float, high: float) -> float:
        """Cost of clamping every rate of a level into the interval [low, high]."""
        return sum(max(low - v, 0.0) + max(v - high, 0.0) for v in block)

    low0 = cuts[0]  # optimal rates never leave [min y, max y]
    table: List[float] = [block_cost(blocks[0], low0, cuts[c]) for c in range(k)]

    for block in blocks[1:]:
        new_table = [float("inf")] * k
        for c in range(k):                      # ceiling of this level
            best = float("inf")
            for c_prev in range(c + 1):         # floor inherited from below
                candidate = table[c_prev] + block_cost(block, cuts[c_prev], cuts[c])
                best = min(best, candidate)
            new_table[c] = best
        table = new_table

    return min(table)


def optimal_repair(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> List[float]:
    """An optimal perturbation d with ||d||_1 = delta(x, y), found by search
    over cut vectors drawn from the observed rates (attainment made explicit)."""
    n = len(x)
    levels: Dict[float, List[int]] = {}
    for i, xi in enumerate(x):
        levels.setdefault(xi, []).append(i)
    blocks: List[List[int]] = [levels[v] for v in sorted(levels)]
    cuts: List[float] = sorted(set(y))

    best_cost = float("inf")
    best_z: List[float] = list(y)
    for choice in product(range(len(cuts)), repeat=len(blocks)):
        if any(a > b for a, b in zip(choice, choice[1:])):
            continue
        z = list(y)
        low = cuts[0]
        cost = 0.0
        for block, c in zip(blocks, choice):
            high = cuts[c]
            for i in block:
                zi = min(max(y[i], low), high)
                z[i] = zi
                cost += abs(zi - y[i])
            low = high
        if cost < best_cost - TOL:
            best_cost, best_z = cost, z
    return [zi - yi for zi, yi in zip(best_z, y)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Triage
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def triage_certified(
    x: Vector, y: Vector, eps: float, big_m: float, eta: float = 0.0
) -> bool:
    """Regime-uniform triage from the single population parameter delta.

    Returns True when  (M/eps)^2 * 2 n R (delta + eta) < C(x, y), which
    certifies wcov(p; x, y) > 0 for EVERY draw regime with eps <= p_i <= M,
    tolerating total measurement error eta in the rates.
    """
    n = len(x)
    kappa = big_m / eps
    budget = kappa ** 2 * 2 * n * footprint_range(x) * (repair_distance(x, y) + eta)
    return budget < concordance_mass(x, y)


def worst_case_wcov(x: Vector, y: Vector, eps: float, big_m: float,
                    trials: int = 20000, seed: int = 0) -> float:
    """Smallest weighted covariance found by random search over admissible
    regimes eps <= p_i <= M, sum p_i = 1.  Used to sanity-check triage."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = len(x)
    worst = float("inf")
    for _ in range(trials):
        raw = [rng.random() for _ in range(n)]
        total = sum(raw)
        p = [r / total for r in raw]
        if all(eps - TOL <= pi <= big_m + TOL for pi in p):
            worst = min(worst, wcov(p, x, y))
    return worst

def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 74)


def report_population(name: str, x: Vector, y: Vector) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    delta = repair_distance(x, y)
    delta_mass = discordance_mass(x, y)
    conc = concordance_mass(x, y)
    n = len(x)
    R = footprint_range(x)
    g = footprint_separation(x)
    env = envelope_repair_cost(x, y)
    cert = pair_certificate_bound(x, y)
    print(f"\n{name}")
    print(f"  x = {list(x)}")
    print(f"  y = {list(y)}")
    print(f"  n = {n}   range R = {R:g}   separation g = {g:g}")
    print(f"  discordance mass  Delta = {delta_mass:g}")
    print(f"  concordance mass  C     = {conc:g}")
    print(f"  repair distance   delta = {delta:g}"
          f"   (certificate {cert:g} <= delta <= envelope {env:g})")
    if g < float("inf"):
        lhs, rhs = 2 * g * delta, 2 * n * R * delta
        ok = lhs <= delta_mass + TOL <= rhs + TOL
        print(f"  two-sided:  2g*delta = {lhs:g}  <=  Delta = {delta_mass:g}"
              f"  <=  2nR*delta = {rhs:g}   [{'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}]")
    return delta, delta_mass

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Vector = Sequence[float]


def repair_distance_exact(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> float:
    """Return delta(x, y) = min { ||y - z||_1 : (x, z) comonotone }.

    Keys sharing a footprint value impose no constraint on one another, so the
    feasible rate vectors z are exactly those for which there are cut values
    t_0 <= t_1 <= ... <= t_{L-1}, one per distinct footprint level in increasing
    order, with every rate of level l lying in [t_{l-1}, t_l].  Given the cuts,
    each coordinate is optimally clamped into its interval, so the total cost
    separates over levels.  The objective is piecewise linear in the cuts, so an
    optimal cut vector may be taken from the multiset of observed rates; a
    dynamic program over (level, cut index) then returns the exact optimum.

    Complexity: O(L * K^2 + n * K) time with L levels and K distinct rates,
    hence O(n^3) in the worst case; O(K) additional space.
    """
    if len(x) == 0:
        return 0.0

    levels: Dict[float, List[float]] = {}
    for xi, yi in zip(x, y):
        levels.setdefault(xi, []).append(yi)
    blocks: List[List[float]] = [levels[v] for v in sorted(levels)]
    cuts: List[float] = sorted(set(y))

    def block_cost(block: Sequence[float], low: float, high: float) -> float:
        return sum(max(low - v, 0.0) + max(v - high, 0.0) for v in block)

    table: List[float] = [block_cost(blocks[0], cuts[0], c) for c in cuts]
    for block in blocks[1:]:
        table = [
            min(table[a] + block_cost(block, cuts[a], cuts[b]) for a in range(b + 1))
            for b in range(len(cuts))
        ]
    return min(table)


def optimal_repair_vector(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> Tuple[List[float], float]:
    """Return an optimal perturbation d and its cost, reconstructing the cuts."""
    levels: Dict[float, List[int]] = {}
    for i, xi in enumerate(x):
        levels.setdefault(xi, []).append(i)
    blocks: List[List[int]] = [levels[v] for v in sorted(levels)]
    cuts: List[float] = sorted(set(y))
    K, L = len(cuts), len(blocks)

    def block_cost(idxs: Sequence[int], low: float, high: float) -> float:
        return sum(max(low - y[i], 0.0) + max(y[i] - high, 0.0) for i in idxs)

    table: List[float] = [block_cost(blocks[0], cuts[0], c) for c in cuts]
    back: List[List[int]] = [[-1] * K for _ in range(L)]
    for l in range(1, L):
        new_table = [float("inf")] * K
        for b in range(K):
            for a in range(b + 1):
                cand = table[a] + block_cost(blocks[l], cuts[a], cuts[b])
                if cand < new_table[b]:
                    new_table[b], back[l][b] = cand, a
        table = new_table

    end = min(range(K), key=lambda b: table[b])
    choice: List[int] = [0] * L
    choice[L - 1] = end
    for l in range(L - 1, 0, -1):
        choice[l - 1] = back[l][choice[l]]

    z: List[float] = list(y)
    low = cuts[0]
    for l, idxs in enumerate(blocks):
        high = cuts[choice[l]]
        for i in idxs:
            z[i] = min(max(y[i], low), high)
        low = high
    d = [zi - yi for zi, yi in zip(z, y)]
    return d, sum(abs(v) for v in d)

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Vector = Sequence[float]


def isotonic_upper_envelope(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> List[float]:
    """The largest rate observed at or strictly below each record's footprint.

    Computed in O(n log n) by sweeping the distinct footprint levels in
    increasing order and maintaining a running maximum of all rates already
    passed.  The result is comonotone with x and dominates y pointwise, so the
    nudge (envelope - y) is always an admissible repair.
    """
    order = sorted(range(len(x)), key=lambda i: x[i])
    env: List[float] = [0.0] * len(x)
    running = -float("inf")
    idx = 0
    while idx < len(order):
        level_end = idx
        while level_end < len(order) and x[order[level_end]] == x[order[idx]]:
            level_end += 1
        level = order[idx:level_end]
        for i in level:
            env[i] = max(running, y[i])
        running = max([running] + [y[i] for i in level])
        idx = level_end
    return env


def envelope_repair(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> Tuple[List[float], float]:
    """The envelope repair vector and its l^1 cost (an upper bound for delta)."""
    env = isotonic_upper_envelope(x, y)
    d = [e - v for e, v in zip(env, y)]
    return d, sum(d)


def charging_certificate(x: Vector, y: Vector) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Produce the pairs of the double-charging argument and verify the bound.

    For each record b at which the envelope spends something, a witness w(b) with
    x[w(b)] < x[b] and y[w(b)] = envelope[b] > y[b] is exhibited; the discordance
    entry D(w(b), b) is at least g * cost(b).  The witness pairs occupy distinct
    columns and their transposes distinct rows, and the two families are
    disjoint, so the charge may be counted twice.  Complexity O(n^2).
    """
    n = len(x)
    env = isotonic_upper_envelope(x, y)
    values = sorted(set(x))
    g = min((b - a for a, b in zip(values, values[1:])), default=float("inf"))

    def disc(a: int, b: int) -> float:
        return max(-(x[a] - x[b]) * (y[a] - y[b]), 0.0)

    charges: List[Tuple[int, int, float, float]] = []
    for b in range(n):
        cost = env[b] - y[b]
        if cost > 0:
            w = max((j for j in range(n) if x[j] < x[b]), key=lambda j: y[j])

    forward = {(w, b) for w, b, _, _ in charges}
    transposed = {(b, w) for w, b, _, _ in charges}
    total_charge = sum(2 * g * c for _, _, c, _ in charges)
    mass = sum(disc(a, b) for a in range(n) for b in range(n))

        "envelope_cost": sum(env[i] - y[i] for i in range(n)),
        "charges": charges,
        "families_disjoint": forward.isdisjoint(transposed),
        "columns_distinct": len({b for _, b in forward}) == len(forward),
        "doubled_charge": total_charge,
        "discordance_mass": mass,
        "bound_holds": total_charge <= mass + 1e-9,

    return [max(y[j] for j in range(len(x)) if j == i or x[j] < x[i])
            for i in range(len(x))]

    best, arg = y[b], b
    for j in range(len(x)):

      levelMap[k].push(y[i]);

      for (var c2 = 0; c2 < cuts.length; c2++) {

          var cand = table[c1] + blockCost(blocks[b], cuts[c1], cuts[c2]);

    var pts = order.map(function (i) {
      return scaleX(xs[i], xLo, xHi) + "," + scaleY(env[i], yLo, yHi);

  "interactive_layout": "# How much would it cost to make your data tell a consistent story?

You have a table with two columns. The first is a **footprint** $x$ — a dose, an
exposure, a firm size, the hours a student studied. The second is a **rate** $y$
— a response rate, a default rate, a score. You want to know whether they move
together.

The usual answer is a correlation coefficient. This page is about a sharper and
more actionable question:

> If the data does not tell a monotone story, **how much would you have to change
> it before it did?**

By the end you will know the answer precisely, you will know exactly how it
relates to the classical pairwise measure of disagreement, and — most
interestingly — you will know precisely what it *cannot* tell you.

---

## 1. Agreement, disagreement, and the two masses

Two records $i$ and $j$ **agree** when footprint and rate move the same way
between them:

$$(x_i - x_j)(y_i - y_j) \ \ge\ 0 .$$

If the product is positive the pair is **concordant**; if negative, **discordant**
— a local contradiction, a place where more footprint bought less rate. A whole
population is **comonotone** when *every* pair is concordant: it is data that
could have come from feeding the footprint through a nondecreasing function.

Add up the contradictions and you get the **discordance mass**; add up the
agreements and you get the **concordance mass**:

$$\Delta(x,y) = \sum_i \sum_j \max\bigl(-(x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j),\, 0\bigr), \qquad
C(x,y) = \sum_i \sum_j \max\bigl((x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j),\, 0\bigr).$$

These are not exotic. They *are* the correlation, before normalisation. Drawing
records with probabilities $p_i$, the weighted covariance ("the dial") has the
classical pairwise form
$\operatorname{wcov}(p;x,y) = \tfrac12\sum_i\sum_j p_ip_j (x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j)$,
and in the uniform case this collapses to a clean identity on $n$ records:

$$2n^2 \cdot \operatorname{wcov} \;=\; C(x,y) - \Delta(x,y).$$

The dial reading is nothing but the balance of agreement against contradiction.

<details>
<summary><b>Why the pairwise form of covariance? (click to expand)</b></summary>

Expand the double sum:
$\tfrac12\sum_{i,j} p_ip_j(x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j)
= \tfrac12\bigl(2\sum_i p_i x_iy_i - 2(\sum_i p_ix_i)(\sum_j p_jy_j)\bigr)$,
using $\sum_i p_i = 1$ throughout. This is [Hoeffding's covariance
identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covariance) in its discrete,
finite-population form, and it is the reason all of the analysis on this page
is pair-based.
</details>

---

## 2. Play with it first

Before any theorem, get the objects into your hands. Drag the rates around and
watch the red discordance arcs appear and vanish; watch the dashed staircase
(the *isotonic upper envelope*, which we meet properly in §5) chase the points;
and watch the numbers on the right update live.

Two presets are worth trying immediately: **Outlier at the bottom** and
**Inversion at the top**. Both need exactly one unit of repair — yet their
discordance masses are $6$ and $2$. Hold that thought; it becomes a theorem in
§8.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

---

## 3. The repair distance

Here is the new object. Nudge the rates: replace $y_i$ by $y_i + d_i$ and pay the
total size of the nudge, $\|d\|_1 = \sum_i |d_i|$. Call $d$ a **repair** if the
nudged population $(x, y+d)$ is comonotone. Then define

$$\delta(x,y) \;=\; \inf\bigl\{ \|d\|_1 \;:\; (x, y+d)\ \text{comonotone} \bigr\}.$$

Geometrically this is the $\ell^1$ distance from the rate vector to the
**isotonic cone** of the footprint — the set of all rate vectors that would have
made the story consistent. It is an
[isotonic regression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isotonic_regression) problem
in the taxicab metric.

Three facts make it respectable:

- **Faithfulness.** $\delta = 0$ exactly when the population is comonotone.
- **Attainment.** The infimum is a minimum: an optimal repair always exists.
- **Stability.** $\delta$ is $1$-Lipschitz in the rates — measurement error of
  total size $\eta$ moves it by at most $\eta$.

<details>
<summary><b>Proofs of the three facts (click to reveal)</b></summary>

*Well-posedness.* The repair set is never empty: taking $d = x - y$ turns the
pair product into $(x_i-x_j)^2 \ge 0$.

*Faithfulness.* One direction is trivial ($d \equiv 0$). For the other, suppose
$x_i < x_j$ but $y_j < y_i$. Any repair $d$ must satisfy
$(y_i + d_i) \le (y_j + d_j)$, hence
$y_i - y_j \le d_j - d_i \le |d_i| + |d_j| \le \|d\|_1$. So every inverted pair is
a **certificate**: $\delta \ge y_i - y_j > 0$.

*Attainment.* The repair set is closed (an intersection of closed half-spaces
translated by $y$) and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is continuous and coercive, so the infimum
may be taken over a compact ball and is achieved.

*Stability.* If $d$ repairs $y'$, then $d + (y' - y)$ repairs $y$, since
$y + (d + y' - y) = y' + d$. Its cost is at most $\|d\|_1 + \|y - y'\|_1$, which
gives $\delta(x,y) \le \delta(x,y') + \|y-y'\|_1$; swap $y, y'$ to get the
Lipschitz bound.
</details>

And here is the sharp contrast with $\Delta$: **the discordance mass has no
Lipschitz estimate at all.** Stretch the footprint to $x = (0,\lambda)$ and move
the rates from $(3,0)$ to $(2,0)$: the displacement is fixed at $1$ while
$\Delta$ moves by $2\lambda$. The repair distance is the *stable* part of the
discordance information.

---

## 4. Computing $\delta$ exactly

The definition is an infimum over a cone, but the problem is a linear program in
disguise, and in fact a short dynamic program. Records that share a footprint
value constrain nothing about each other, so the feasible repaired rate vectors
are exactly those admitting a nondecreasing sequence of **cuts**, one per
footprint level, with every rate at a level clamped into its interval. The
objective is piecewise linear, so optimal cuts can be taken from the multiset of
observed rates — and then a table over (level, cut) finishes the job.

{{algorithm:0}}

---

## 5. The lower bound, and a picture of its proof

The engine of the theory is a single explicit repair. For each record $b$, let

$$\hat y_b \;=\; \max\{\, y_j \;:\; x_j < x_b \ \text{or}\ j = b \,\}$$

be the largest rate observed **at or strictly below** $b$'s footprint. This
**isotonic upper envelope** is automatically comonotone with the footprint, so
$d = \hat y - y \ge 0$ is a legitimate repair, and the total arrow length in the
picture below is an upper bound for $\delta$.

The charging argument is the pretty part. Wherever the envelope spends something
at $b$, its value is realised by a *witness* record $w(b)$ sitting strictly lower
in footprint and strictly higher in rate. If the distinct footprint values are
$g$-separated, that witness pair carries at least $g$ times the spend. Distinct
records give distinct witness pairs — the pair $(w(b), b)$ remembers $b$ in its
second slot — so the charges live in distinct **columns** of the discordance
table and may be summed with no double counting.

{{visualization:2}}

{{algorithm:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>Where does the extra factor of $2$ come from? (click to reveal)</b></summary>

The discordance table is symmetric: $D(a,b) = D(b,a)$. So besides the witness
family $\{(w(b), b)\}$ there is the transposed family $\{(b, w(b))\}$, carrying
exactly the same mass. The two families are **disjoint**: an overlap
$(w(b), b) = (b', w(b'))$ would force $x_{b'} < x_b$ *and* $x_b < x_{b'}$. So every
charge can be counted twice, and

$$2\,g\,\delta(x,y) \;\le\; \Delta(x,y),$$

with no dependence whatsoever on the number of records. The constant $2$ is
*exactly* optimal: for $x = (0,1)$, $y = (3,0)$ one has $g = 1$, $\delta = 3$,
$\Delta = 6$, and the inequality is an equality.
</details>

---

## 6. The upper bound, and the conjecture that fails

In the other direction, take any repair $d$. Comonotonicity of $(x, y+d)$ gives,
pair by pair,

$$-(x_i-x_j)(y_i-y_j) \;\le\; (x_i-x_j)(d_i-d_j) \;\le\; R\,(|d_i| + |d_j|),$$

where $R$ bounds the footprint spread. Summing over all $n^2$ ordered pairs,
each coordinate $|d_k|$ is charged $2n$ times, so

$$\Delta(x,y) \;\le\; 2\,n\,R\,\delta(x,y).$$

That factor $n$ looks like a proof artifact. It is not. The natural
dimension-free conjecture

$$\delta^2 \;\le\; \Delta \;\le\; 2\,\delta\,R$$

is false on **both** sides, and for two entirely different reasons.

<details>
<summary><b>Left side: a degree obstruction (click to reveal)</b></summary>

Both $\Delta$ and $\delta$ are positively homogeneous of degree **one** in the
rates: scale every $y_i$ by $t > 0$ and both scale by $t$. But $\delta^2$ scales by
$t^2$. So for $x = (0,1)$ and $y_t = (3t, 0)$ we get $\delta = 3t$, $\Delta = 6t$
and $\delta^2/\Delta = 3t/2 \to \infty$. No inequality of that shape can survive;
any correct comparison must be degree-matched.
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Right side: a dimension obstruction (click to reveal)</b></summary>

Discordance aggregates over $\Theta(n^2)$ pairs, but a single coordinate move can
repair all of them. On $x = (0,1,\dots,n-1)$ with $y = (1,0,\dots,0)$ — one unit
outlier at the bottom — we have $\delta = 1$, $R = n-1$, and $\Delta = n(n-1)$
exactly. So $\Delta / (R\delta) = n$ is unbounded, and no bound
$\Delta \le C R \delta$ can hold. The same family shows the correct bound
$2nR\delta$ overshoots by *exactly* a factor of two, so its shape is right.
</details>

{{visualization:1}}

Putting the halves together gives the main theorem:

$$\boxed{\;2\,g\,\delta(x,y) \;\le\; \Delta(x,y) \;\le\; 2\,n\,R\,\delta(x,y)\;}$$

for a $g$-separated footprint of range at most $R$ on $n$ records. Every
population lives in that wedge, and both walls are touched:

{{visualization:0}}

---

## 7. What it is for: triage in one number

Suppose you want to certify that a study will show a positive association — that
$\operatorname{wcov}(p;x,y) > 0$ — and you want the guarantee to hold *no matter
how the sample was drawn*, as long as no record is vanishingly rare or
overwhelmingly common: say $\varepsilon \le p_i \le M$, with conditioning number
$\kappa = M/\varepsilon$.

Splitting the pairwise covariance gives
$2\operatorname{wcov} \ge \varepsilon^2 C - M^2 \Delta$, so $M^2\Delta < \varepsilon^2 C$
suffices. Feeding in the upper bound turns this into a rule in **one
interpretable parameter**:

$$\kappa^2 \cdot 2\,n\,R\,\delta(x,y) \;<\; C(x,y)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{wcov}(p;x,y) > 0 \ \text{in every admissible regime}.$$

A population that is cheap to repair cannot be triaged away by any conditioning
number. And because $\delta$ is $1$-Lipschitz, measurement error of total size
$\eta$ is absorbed simply by replacing $\delta$ with $\delta + \eta$ — an estimate
that would be impossible with $\Delta$.

{{algorithm:2}}

Read the same inequality backwards and the repair distance becomes a *budget
line inside the dial itself*:

$$2n^2\operatorname{wcov} \;\le\; C(x,y) - g\,\delta(x,y),
\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad
g\,\delta(x,y) \;\le\; C(x,y) - 2n^2\operatorname{wcov}.$$

Every unit of repair a population needs is subtracted, one for one, from the
largest signal it could possibly display; conversely, a strong observed signal
certifies that the underlying data is cheap to fix.

{{demo:1}}

---

## 8. The thing you cannot compress

It would be lovely to declare $\delta$ a replacement for $\Delta$. It is not, and
the obstruction is exactly the pair of presets you played with in §2. On the same
footprint $x = (0,1,2)$:

| rates | repair distance $\delta$ | discordance mass $\Delta$ |
|---|---|---|
| $(1,0,0)$ — outlier at the bottom | $1$ | $6$ |
| $(0,1,0)$ — inversion at the top | $1$ | $2$ |

**The discordance mass is not a function of the repair distance.** An $\ell^1$
repair records only *how far* rates must move; the discordance mass also records
*how many pairs* each misplaced rate offends, and that count depends on where in
the footprint order the offence sits. An outlier at the extreme contradicts
everything; an inversion between neighbours contradicts one thing. Both cost one
unit of repair.

Three consequences: the two-sided comparison can never be sharpened to an
identity; the one-parameter triage rule is genuinely *sufficient only*; and the
pairwise table is irreducible — no $\ell^1$ repair statistic can stand in for it.

---

## 9. Run everything yourself

The full numerical companion below reproduces every claim on this page: the
witness populations and their exact values, attainment of the constant $2$, the
degree and dimension obstructions, the uniform pair identity, the dial cap, the
triage rule with and without measurement error, and a randomised stress test of
the sandwich over thousands of populations.

{{demo:0}}

---

## Where next

Three concrete directions are open. First, an **exact normal form**: prove that
some optimal repair has all coordinates drawn from the multiset of observed
rates, turning $\delta$ into a fully computable statistic. Second, a **weighted
repair distance** $\sum_i p_i|d_i|$, which should reduce the conditioning
dependence in the triage rule from $\kappa^2$ to $\kappa$, because the charging
argument is already in the disjoint-family form that such a reweighting needs.
Third — the most tempting — **which repair costs recover the pairwise data?**
Weights depending on a record's rank in the footprint order can see part of the
"how many pairs" count that the plain $\ell^1$ cost misses. Is there a cost for
which the comparison becomes an identity, or is the irreducibility absolute?

# The comonotone repair distance and the discordance mass

Third cycle of the `UniformDial` thread (see `Combinatorics.UniformDialDrawInvariance` for
the pairwise identity and `Combinatorics.UniformDialRegimeHomotopy` for the concordance
budget and the QS triage rule).

A population `(x, y)` on a finite key set `ι` is *comonotone* when no pair of keys is
discordant.  The regime-free quantity governing the triage rule of the previous cycle is
the **discordance mass** `Δ = discordanceMass x y`.  Here we introduce a genuinely
different, *geometric* measure of non-comonotonicity:

> `repairDist x y = inf { ‖d‖₁ : (x, y + d) is comonotone }`,

the least ℓ¹ perturbation of the rates that removes every discordant pair.  This is exactly
the ℓ¹ distance from `y` to the isotonic cone of the preorder induced by `x`, so the object
is an ℓ¹ isotonic-regression problem attached to the population.

## What is proved

* `repairDist_nonneg`, `repairDist_le_of_mem`, `le_repairDist` — the infimum is well posed
  (the repair set is never empty: `d = x - y` always works).
* `violation_le_repairDist` — every discordant pair is a certificate: the size of its
  rate inversion is a lower bound for the repair distance.
* `repairDist_eq_zero_iff_comonotone` — the repair distance is a faithful defect measure.
* `discordanceMass_le_repairDist` — **upper bound**: `Δ ≤ 2 · |ι| · range(x) · δ`.
* `repairDist_le_discordanceMass` — **lower bound**: `g · δ ≤ Δ` whenever the distinct
  footprint values are `g`-separated.  The proof is constructive and dimension-free: the
  upper envelope `isoUp` of `y` along `x` is an explicit admissible repair whose cost at
  each key is charged to a *distinct column* of the discordance matrix.
* `repair_discordance_two_sided` — the two bounds packaged as a two-sided comparison.
* `dial_pos_of_repair_distance` — **QS triage with a single population parameter**: the
  dial is strictly positive in *every* regime with mass ratio `κ = M/ε` as soon as
  `κ² · 2 |ι| · range(x) · δ < C`.

The naive dimension-free forms of the two inequalities are *false*, and we prove it with
explicit finite populations:

* `no_quadratic_lower_bound` — `δ² ≤ Δ` fails (`x = (0,1)`, `y = (3,0)`: `δ = 3`, `Δ = 6`).
  The two sides have different scaling degrees in `y`, so no such bound can hold.
* `no_dimension_free_upper_bound` — `Δ ≤ 2 δ range(x)` fails (`x = (0,1,2)`, `y = (1,0,0)`:
  `δ = 1`, `range = 2`, `Δ = 6 > 4`).  The factor `|ι|` in `discordanceMass_le_repairDist`

* `no_lower_bound_constant_above_two` — the constant in `g · δ ≤ Δ` is optimal up to `2`.
* `discordance_not_determined_by_repairDist` — two populations with the *same* footprint

import Combinatorics.UniformDialRegimeHomotopy

open Finset

namespace Catalog.UniformDial

variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]

/-! ### The repair distance -/

/-- ℓ¹ size of a perturbation of the rates. -/
noncomputable def l1norm (d : ι → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i, |d i|

lemma l1norm_nonneg (d : ι → ℝ) : 0 ≤ l1norm d :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => abs_nonneg _

/-- The admissible repairs of a population: the perturbations of the rate vector that
make the population comonotone. -/
def RepairSet (x y : ι → ℝ) : Set (ι → ℝ) := {d | Comonotone x (fun i => y i + d i)}

omit [Fintype ι] in
/-- `d = x - y` is always an admissible repair, so the repair set is never empty. -/
lemma sub_mem_RepairSet (x y : ι → ℝ) : (fun i => x i - y i) ∈ RepairSet x y := by
  intro i j
  have h : (x i - x j) * ((y i + (x i - y i)) - (y j + (x j - y j))) = (x i - x j) ^ 2 := by
    ring
  rw [h]
  exact sq_nonneg _

/-- **The comonotone repair distance**: the least ℓ¹ perturbation of the rates that
removes every discordant pair. -/
noncomputable def repairDist (x y : ι → ℝ) : ℝ := sInf (l1norm '' RepairSet x y)

lemma repairImage_nonempty (x y : ι → ℝ) : (l1norm '' RepairSet x y).Nonempty :=
  ⟨_, ⟨_, sub_mem_RepairSet x y, rfl⟩⟩

lemma repairImage_bddBelow (x y : ι → ℝ) : BddBelow (l1norm '' RepairSet x y) := by
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  rintro _ ⟨d, -, rfl⟩
  exact l1norm_nonneg d

lemma repairDist_nonneg (x y : ι → ℝ) : 0 ≤ repairDist x y := by
  refine le_csInf (repairImage_nonempty x y) ?_
  rintro _ ⟨d, -, rfl⟩
  exact l1norm_nonneg d

/-- Every admissible repair bounds the repair distance from above. -/
lemma repairDist_le_of_mem {x y d : ι → ℝ} (hd : d ∈ RepairSet x y) :
    repairDist x y ≤ l1norm d :=
  csInf_le (repairImage_bddBelow x y) ⟨d, hd, rfl⟩

/-- A quantity dominated by the cost of every admissible repair bounds the repair
distance from below. -/
lemma le_repairDist {x y : ι → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (h : ∀ d ∈ RepairSet x y, c ≤ l1norm d) :
    c ≤ repairDist x y := by
  refine le_csInf (repairImage_nonempty x y) ?_
  rintro _ ⟨d, hd, rfl⟩
  exact h d hd

/-- Two coordinates of a perturbation never cost more than its ℓ¹ size. -/
lemma two_abs_le_l1norm (d : ι → ℝ) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    |d i| + |d j| ≤ l1norm d := by
  classical
  have hsub : ({i, j} : Finset ι) ⊆ univ := subset_univ _
  have hpair : ∑ k ∈ ({i, j} : Finset ι), |d k| = |d i| + |d j| := by
    rw [Finset.sum_pair hij]
  calc |d i| + |d j| = ∑ k ∈ ({i, j} : Finset ι), |d k| := hpair.symm
    _ ≤ ∑ k, |d k| :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg hsub (fun k _ _ => abs_nonneg _)
    _ = l1norm d := rfl

/-- **Every discordant pair is a certificate.**  If key `i` has the strictly smaller
footprint, then any repair must pay at least the size of the rate inversion `y i - y j`
(the statement is vacuous when that quantity is nonpositive). -/
theorem violation_le_repairDist {x y : ι → ℝ} {i j : ι} (hx : x i < x j) :
    y i - y j ≤ repairDist x y := by
  refine le_repairDist ?_
  intro d hd
  have hcom := hd i j
  have hne : i ≠ j := fun h => absurd (h ▸ hx) (lt_irrefl _)
  have hxneg : x i - x j < 0 := by linarith
  have hz : y i + d i ≤ y j + d j := by nlinarith [hcom]
  have h1 : y i - y j ≤ d j - d i := by linarith
  have h2 : d j - d i ≤ |d i| + |d j| := by
    have := neg_abs_le (d i)
    have := le_abs_self (d j)
    linarith
  exact h1.trans (h2.trans (two_abs_le_l1norm d hne))

/-- The repair distance vanishes exactly on comonotone populations: it is a faithful

theorem repairDist_eq_zero_iff_comonotone (x y : ι → ℝ) :

    push_neg at hij
    -- a discordant pair produces a strictly positive certificate

    · have hy : y j < y i := by nlinarith
      have := violation_le_repairDist (y := y) hx
      rw [h] at this
      linarith
    · rw [hx] at hij; simp at hij
    · have hy : y i < y j := by nlinarith
      have := violation_le_repairDist (y := y) hx
      rw [h] at this
      linarith
  · intro h
    refine le_antisymm ?_ (repairDist_nonneg x y)
    have hmem : (fun _ : ι => (0 : ℝ)) ∈ RepairSet x y := by
      intro i j
      simpa using h i j
    have := repairDist_le_of_mem hmem
    simpa [l1norm] using this

/-! ### Upper bound: the discordance mass is controlled by the repair distance -/

lemma sum_pair_abs (d : ι → ℝ) :
    ∑ i, ∑ j, (|d i| + |d j|) = 2 * (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * l1norm d := by
  have h1 : ∀ i : ι, ∑ _j : ι, |d i| = (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * |d i| := by
    intro i
    rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have : ∑ i, ∑ j, (|d i| + |d j|)
      = ∑ i : ι, ((Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * |d i| + l1norm d) := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, h1 i]
    rfl
  rw [this, Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ,
    nsmul_eq_mul]
  simp only [l1norm]
  ring

omit [Fintype ι] in
/-- Pointwise bound: the discordant part of a pair product is at most `range(x)` times the
ℓ¹ cost the repair spends on the two keys. -/
lemma discordant_term_le {x y d : ι → ℝ} (hd : d ∈ RepairSet x y) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R)
    (hx : ∀ i j, |x i - x j| ≤ R) (i j : ι) :
    max (-((x i - x j) * (y i - y j))) 0 ≤ R * (|d i| + |d j|) := by
  have hcom := hd i j
  have key : -((x i - x j) * (y i - y j)) ≤ (x i - x j) * (d i - d j) := by nlinarith [hcom]
  have habs : (x i - x j) * (d i - d j) ≤ R * (|d i| + |d j|) := by
    have h1 : (x i - x j) * (d i - d j) ≤ |x i - x j| * |d i - d j| := by
      have := le_abs_self ((x i - x j) * (d i - d j))
      rwa [abs_mul] at this
    have h2 : |d i - d j| ≤ |d i| + |d j| := abs_sub _ _
    have h3 : |x i - x j| * |d i - d j| ≤ R * (|d i| + |d j|) :=
      mul_le_mul (hx i j) h2 (abs_nonneg _) hR
    linarith
  have hnn : 0 ≤ R * (|d i| + |d j|) :=
    mul_nonneg hR (by positivity)
  exact max_le (le_trans key habs) hnn

/-- Every admissible repair bounds the discordance mass. -/
lemma discordanceMass_le_of_mem {x y d : ι → ℝ} (hd : d ∈ RepairSet x y) {R : ℝ}
    (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hx : ∀ i j, |x i - x j| ≤ R) :
    discordanceMass x y ≤ 2 * (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * R * l1norm d := by
  have hstep : discordanceMass x y ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, R * (|d i| + |d j|) := by
    refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => ?_
    exact discordant_term_le hd hR hx i j
  have hsum : ∑ i, ∑ j, R * (|d i| + |d j|) = R * ∑ i, ∑ j, (|d i| + |d j|) := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [hsum, sum_pair_abs d] at hstep
  linarith [hstep]

/-- **Upper bound (corrected form).**  The discordance mass is at most
`2 · |ι| · range(x)` times the comonotone repair distance.  The population-size factor is
genuinely needed — see `no_dimension_free_upper_bound`. -/
theorem discordanceMass_le_repairDist (x y : ι → ℝ) {R : ℝ} (hx : ∀ i j, |x i - x j| ≤ R) :
    discordanceMass x y ≤ 2 * (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * R * repairDist x y := by

  · have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) = 0 := by
      simp [Fintype.card_eq_zero]

  · obtain ⟨i0⟩ := hι
    have hR : 0 ≤ R := by simpa using hx i0 i0

      fun d hd => discordanceMass_le_of_mem hd hR hx
    set c : ℝ := 2 * (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * R with hc
    have hc0 : 0 ≤ c := by
      have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg _
      positivity
    rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hc0 with hzero | hpos
    · have hd0 := hkey _ (sub_mem_RepairSet x y)
      rw [← hzero] at hd0 ⊢
      have : discordanceMass x y ≤ 0 := by simpa using hd0
      have h2 := discordanceMass_nonneg x y
